(Chapter 176/177)

After obtaining Baku's number through an unknown process, Billy tracks him down and arrives at the Abandoned Building. He senses the bloodshed and death that the building was host to, perceiving the battles that had occurred within it previously. After noticing the arrangement of the keys on the first and second floor, Billy concludes that Baku is trying to play a game of altered 'Nim' with him as a test of wits. He surmises that Baku and himself will alternate between turning the keys on one of three floors at a time, in a variation of Nim called Miyama Kuzushi ('Destroy Three Mountains').

Billy remarks that games such as this typically involve a special calculation, and so the winner of the game (assuming both play perfectly) can be calculated from the start. He goes on to reason that the number of keys on each floor can be converted to binary, and using the numerical sum of the binary values, he can determine whether the game is able to be won or not (all even numbers in sum on Billy's turn means impossible to win if Baku plays perfectly). Taking all of this into account, Billy deduces that if he is to be able to still win this game conventionally, the third floor must not have 3 keys. This is because if the arrangement was 3/5/3, since all 3 on the first floor and 2 on the second floor have been turned, 3 are left on the second and third floors respectively. 3 in binary is 11, 11+11=22, and as both digits are even on Billy's turn, it is theoretically impossible for him to win.

However, Billy improvises, using his world-renowned spork to link all three unturned keys on the second floor. As such, when he turns 2 keys on the top floor, Baku logically turns 2 on the second floor, but actually turns all 3 in the process, leaving the last key to Billy. Despite this, Billy actually already knew that the keys weren't linked to Baku's room, and that he would let him in anyways once Billy proved his intelligence. All of this effort was so that Billy could tell Baku that he already knew his plan to use the L-File to seize the 50 Billion Yen required for Surpassing The Leader, declare that Ideal will steal it from him, and then leave. Pure aura 🥹.

Explanation of Billy's Manipulation of Sweeper Yakou and Fake Death Plan:

The initial aim of the strategy begins during Billy's first confrontation with Kakerou to test their strength, encountering Mizue Yuuko (Kakerou's Minister of Foreign Affairs) and battling her until Sweeper Yakou (Jouichi) emerged. Billy did not have to risk himself by fighting Yakou, since he had already prepared an insurance of the Police breaching the intervention ban issued by Kakerou and allowing him to escape, but he chose to anyway.

By creating a scene with Kakerou, Billy strains Police relations with Kakerou even more, aiding in his later plans during Tower of Karma. The fight with Yakou served two purposes: to once again test the brute power of the upper echelons of Kakerou forces, but more importantly, to create a situation where the Sweeper would try to pursue him.

Billy was already aware that Kakerou knew Ideal was trying to challenge Surpassing The Leader, which directly relates him to Usogui, especially considering Ideal's involvement with the missiles during the Terrorist Mine gamble. Using this, he plans to use Sweeper Yakou to indirectly gather information about what Baku is doing, which ties into his strategy to make him use the L-File and seize the 50 Billion Yen and Karamete on his behalf.

Fast forwarding to when Amako confronts Baku after the Paper Labyrinth gamble, Billy had stolen and returned the L-File to Amako in order to create a feud with him, making him more inclined to use it as a wager during the Minotaur Labyrinth gamble, and also alerting the Private Funeral Division to its potential exposure, which aligns with Billy's scheme to force Baku into a Kakerou match with Suteguma at the Empire Tower (since the PFD would be quickly prepared to take down the broadcast otherwise), which in itself is another one of Billy's schemes.

After this, Amako instructs the Public Funeral Division (essentially a fake Private Funeral Division used for smaller tasks like arresting those who have had their alibis taken) to watch over Billy and Martin. While Amako waits for Kaji's arrest, Billy is being driven around by the Public FD nearby, and spots Karl around a corner. This is where Billy orchestrates his fake death plan, escaping from the Public FD to chase after Karl.

Billy was aware that Karl was staying with his bodyguard from the Abandoned Mine, Kyara, who he also knew was a former Kakerou referee. Using these premises, Billy could conclude that Kakerou, and hence Sweeper Yakou would be hunting Kyara down, therefore it is highly likely that Yakou would intercept him during the fight. Since Billy has already engineered a situation involving the L-File with Amako, all he needs to do now is alert Baku to its existence.

We can infer that after Kyara's bike attack on the car that Billy told Martin to call for men from Ideal and have them pose as members of the Private Funeral Division, and this allows him to fake his own death when Yakou inevitably gets involved, meaning that Kakerou will stop pursuing Billy thereafter.

Before he fakes his death though, he needs to engage in a fight with Kyara; since both himself and Kyara are high-value Kakerou targets, he predicts the Sweeper's arrival, and as expected, he reveals Baku's current predicament at the Police Department, as well as Kyara's involvement with Baku, allowing Billy to proceed to the next stage of his scheme.

Knowing that Kyara, Kaji and Karl were now working under Usogui, he only had to wait until Ideal's men arrived to fabricate a situation where he could indirectly hint at the existence of L-File to Baku through his three allies, claiming that the Private Funeral Division must suspect him of copying the L-File to hide the fact that revealing its existence was his intention.

The fake PFD then shoots Billy with special sedative/tranquillizing bullets to fake his death, leading to Billy lying motionless until Kyara and Yakou escape. It is possible that Martin credits Amako for this ploy because he is trying to hide the fact that he knows his true identity as Nicolas and his sleep condition.

The most likely sequence of events is that Martin was the one who prepared the sedative bullets since he knows about Billy's condition, and that he would quickly recover since he can't sleep, but of course Martin wants to conceal this until he gets the chance to kill Nicolas, so fabricates a story in which Amako prepared the bullets instead.
